recognize_zh: 中央細胞的核分成三葉、染色質粗糙，淡粉紅細胞質中散布比平常明顯的紫色顆粒，屬分節嗜中性球（segmented neutrophil）並帶輕度毒性顆粒（toxic granulation）。
features: Mature granulocyte about 1.5 times red cell diameter
Nucleus segmented into three lobes connected by thin chromatin strands, with coarsely clumped chromatin
Pale pink cytoplasm containing scattered purple granules that are somewhat more prominent than usual (mild toxic granulation)
No Döhle bodies or cytoplasmic vacuoles clearly identified at this resolution
Background normocytic red cells; one red cell at upper right shows fine punctate dark dots, and scattered platelets are present
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mostly normocytic, normochromic red cells with adequate-appearing platelets. A mature neutrophil in the center has a three-lobed nucleus with coarse chromatin and pale cytoplasm containing scattered purple granules that are slightly coarser and more conspicuous than normal. Definite vacuolization or Döhle bodies are not appreciated. An isolated red cell at the upper right contains fine punctate inclusions of uncertain significance. Findings are consistent with a mature segmented neutrophil with mild toxic granulation, as may be seen in infection, inflammation or growth factor therapy.

ddx.vs: Normal neutrophil granules are fine, lilac and barely visible, whereas toxic granules are coarser and darker purple as seen here.
Alder-Reilly granules are large dark inclusions present in all granulocytes (and often lymphocytes) persistently, without clinical infection.
Hypersegmentation requires six or more lobes (or >5% with five lobes), whereas this cell has only three lobes.
